traditions.label: Cistercian
traditions.scope: Printed missals of the Cistercian Order
traditions.coverage_note: Corrected printed witnesses of 1487, 1606 and 1657; bounded Canon and Pentecost comparisons alongside three complete Ordinary prayer pairs. Publication, mandates and reception remain distinct.

sources.title: Missale Cisterciense (Strasbourg, Johann Grüninger, 1487)
sources.inspection: BSB 2 Inc.c.a. 1921, bsb 00044164: opening mandate canvas 6 dated 3 October 1486; execution canvas 7; Canon opening and Memento canvas 225; Confiteor canvas 234; colophon canvas 423 dated pridie nonas Septembris 1487 (4 September). Complete 428-page PDF acquired and hashed, with critical page images retained.
sources.limitations: Selected critical pages inspected, not a complete-book collation. PDF has a provider cover before 427 source canvases and no usable historical-text layer. The 1486 mandate and 1487 publication do not establish uniform local reception.

stages.label: 1487 corrected Cistercian missal
stages.scope: Printed order missal prepared under the 1486 commission for uniform corrected liturgical books.
stages.witness_label: Missale Cisterciense, Strasbourg, Johann Grüninger, 1487; BSB 2 Inc.c.a. 1921, bsb 00044164; USUARIUM 423
stages.summary: The opening mandate of Johannes abbot of Cîteaux orders corrected missals, breviaries and psalters under general-chapter authority and directs houses to acquire and conform their books. The colophon dates this printing to 4 September 1487. Its Memento lacks two clauses found in 1606, while both Canon openings retain the king among named intercessions.

evidence.claim: Mandate dated 3 October 1486; corrected books and order-wide uniformity are prescribed.
Publication date 1487, pridie nonas Septembris (4 September).

evidence.locus: Canon opening and Memento, BSB canvas 225
evidence.claim: Earlier paired Canon wording read directly from the page image.

stages.limitations: Already a corrected printed state, not a proxy for every medieval Cistercian manuscript. The 1486 mandate is a separate event from 1487 publication; the date of first introduction of individual clauses is unestablished. Retained source images and bounded readings do not provide a checked canonical text transcription.
stages.reception: The mandate directs houses to acquire and use corrected books; no house-by-house reception chronology has been established.

stages.label: 1606 Romanizing Cistercian missal
stages.scope: Printed order missal implementing Roman conformity in the Canon while retaining Cistercian usages elsewhere.
stages.witness_label: Missale ad usum Sacri Ordinis Cisterciensis, Paris, Dionysia Cavellat, 1606; BSB 2 Liturg. 205 a
stages.summary: The 1606 Annotanda attributes full Roman conformity in the Canon to the 1601 and 1605 general chapters, and conformity elsewhere only as proper Cistercian use allows. The printed Ordinary still has a short Confiteor, a combined Suscipe Trinitas offering, and Orate/Dominus sit response.

evidence.claim: Explicit reforms of the 1601 and 1605 chapters; full conformity in the Canon, limited conformity elsewhere.
Three bounded prayer units directly transcribed from page images.

stages.limitations: This is already a revised state, not a proxy for all medieval Cistercian practice. The exact 1606 witness has now been split from the earlier broad printed-witness cluster. No claim that every decree of 1601 or 1605 was fully received locally.
stages.reception: The book identifies itself as for the Cistercian Order and invokes chapter authority; no monastery-by-monastery reception census has been made.

stages.label: 1657 further Roman correction
stages.scope: Printed Cistercian missal following the 1651 commission; a substantially Romanized Ordinary while retaining order-specific material.
stages.witness_label: Missale Cisterciense iuxta Romani recogniti correctionem, Paris, Sebastianus and Gabriel Cramoisy, 1657; Krzeszów copy, FIDES 3755
stages.summary: The Ordinary enlarges the Confiteor with named saints including Bernard and triple culpa; replaces the old Orate and response; prints separate host and chalice offerings and a revised Suscipe Trinitas after Lavabo. The Monitum reports reordered Pentecost-to-Advent Sunday Masses and Roman rubrics, but expressly retains differences in the graduals.

evidence.claim: The general chapter held in May 1651 authorized three learned men to correct the books; the 1655 mandate extends the printing privilege.
Primary description of the new revision; retained graduals prevent complete Roman imitation.
Three complete paired prayers and their position in the offertory read from images.

stages.limitations: The 1651 commission, 1655 mandate, and 1657 publication are distinct dates. The inspected 1655 instrument is not a universal effective-date decree. The Monitum historical catalogue of earlier defects must not all be assigned specifically to 1606.
stages.reception: The Cistercian superior authorizes the edition and printing monopoly; this is evidence of intended order use, not uniform local implementation.

transitions.summary: The 1606 Memento includes all the faithful and an explicit offering on behalf of those remembered, clauses absent from the 1487 printing.

changes.locus_before: 1487 BSB canvas 225, right column, complete Memento visible

evidence.claim: The 1487 reading proceeds directly from circumstantium through quorum to qui tibi offerunt.
The 1606 reading adds omniumque fidelium and pro quibus tibi offerimus, vel.
Direct comparison of the complete Memento context.
The 1606 edition describes Roman conformity under the 1601 and 1605 chapters; the compared wording is directly visible.

transitions.limitations: This bounded witness comparison is not a complete Ordinary collation. The 1487 printing is not established as the direct exemplar of 1606. Neither the first introduction of either clause nor an intermediate effective date is inferred. Latin excerpts normalize long-s, expand typographic abbreviations and omit accent marks for the bounded comparison.

transitions.summary: Further Romanization changes three complete Ordinary prayer units and the printed Holy Saturday ending: expanded Confiteor, replaced Orate and response, revised and relocated Suscipe Trinitas, and relocation of Spiritum nobis from a Postcommunio heading to the integrated Vespers sequence. A paired Pentecost Sunday example also changes numbering and Gospel while retaining the epistle, gradual and Alleluia.

evidence.claim: Second Sunday pairs the 1 John 4 epistle and retained chants with Luke 16.
First Sunday pairs the same epistle and chant incipits with Luke 6. The Monitum describes the broader Pentecost-to-Advent rearrangement and retained graduals.
The earlier state already implements Roman conformity under the chapters of 1601 and 1605.
The 1651 chapter ordered renewed revision; the editor claims a closer Roman form but retains differences in the graduals.

transitions.limitations: Text-collated applies to three complete prayer units, their local rubrics, and the Holy Saturday ending on the identified pages. The Holy Saturday quotations are bounded excerpts, not complete service transcriptions. Wider calendar, lectionary, and chant changes have primary-description evidence and have not been exhaustively collated. This is an institutional Cistercian revision relation, not proof that the 1657 typesetter directly copied this particular 1606 edition. All six complete prayer bodies have passed independent image review; one printed accent was corrected. The Holy Saturday rubrics remain a separate bounded review. A further bounded example directly compares 1606 Second Sunday and 1657 First Sunday after Pentecost: numbering and Gospel change, while the identified epistle and chant units are retained. These are descriptive incipits and appointments, not complete literal transcriptions of the propers. This supports one instance of the Monitum claim without verifying all Sundays or comparing every chant against a Roman exemplar.

gaps.missing: Complete paired 1487 or medieval Ordinary against 1606, and visually verified original chapter acts of 1601 and 1605; the 1487 publication and mandate and a bounded Memento comparison are now documented.
gaps.next_source: BSB bsb00044164 remaining Ordinary pages; Canivez Statuta volume VII and original chapter-act witnesses for 1601 and 1605; BL Add. 46203 and Fribourg L 158.
gaps.consequence: Cannot treat 1606 as an unchanged medieval baseline or date the first introduction of every Romanizing element.

gaps.missing: Complete collation of all Pentecost-to-Advent readings, new feasts, retained graduals against Roman exemplars, and the Holy Week sequence.
gaps.next_source: 1606 BSB bsb 10496382 temporale and calendar; 1657 FIDES 3755 Monitum and the complete corresponding sections.
gaps.consequence: One paired Pentecost Sunday example now has direct image evidence alongside three complete Ordinary prayer pairs and the bounded Holy Saturday ending. The complete seasonal and calendar reform remains uncollated.

gaps.missing: Local reception chronology and binding effective-date instruments.
gaps.next_source: Cistercian general chapter acts from 1651 onward, house book inventories, and correction orders.
gaps.consequence: Publication does not prove instant uniform replacement throughout the Order.
